title: Relative affine space
statement:
For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an index set $I$, define the relative affine space, with its first projection to $S$, by
$$
\mathbb A^I_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbb Z[T_i:i\in I]\bigr)
$$
using the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] and affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Here $R[T_i:i\in I]$ is the commutative polynomial algebra: its polynomials are finite sums of monomials, each monomial involving finitely many variables, even when $I$ is infinite. On an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$, the inverse image of $V$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_i:i\in I])$ over $V$; on a principal restriction $D(a)\subseteq V$ the restriction morphism is induced contravariantly by the coefficient map $R[T_i:i\in I]\to R_a[T_i:i\in I]$, fixing every $T_i$, where $R_a=R[1/a]$.

For an integer $n\geq0$, take $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and write $\mathbb A^n_S$. Equivalently, there is a canonical isomorphism over $S$
$$
\mathbb A^n_S\cong\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n})\bigr).
$$
Here $\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n}$ is the finite direct sum of $n$ copies of the structure module, with its ordered standard basis [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The symmetric algebra sheaf is the sheafification construction of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]; its quasi-coherence and affine sections are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine]. Relative spectrum has the meaning and compatible affine restrictions of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec]. The displayed isomorphism is the one whose affine ring identifications send each standard-basis generator to the corresponding $T_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial]. In finite rank the fibre-product definition is also the definition of [def-sbc-affine-space].

proof.text: For the finite-rank comparison put $F=\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n}$. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, its inclusions and projections identify its sections with $R^n$, with the standard basis; the corresponding sheaf on $U$ is $\widetilde{R^n}$. Thus $F$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent], including $n=0$. Let $B$ be its explicitly sheafified symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine]: $B$ is quasi-coherent and its canonical map $\operatorname{Sym}_R(R^n)\to B(U)$ is an algebra isomorphism. It is an algebra map by construction and is bijective by the cited statement.

On each affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, compose the inverse of the symmetric-algebra polynomial isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] with the isomorphism of step 1. This identifies $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ with $B(U)$, sending $T_i$ to the image of the standard section $e_i$. For an inclusion of affine opens the two resulting maps agree on coefficients and on every $T_i$: restrictions of $F$ fix its standard basis, and the restrictions and sheafification unit defining $B$ commute [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. Since coefficients and variables generate the polynomial ring, the maps agree on every polynomial. The affine opens form a basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. On any open $W$, map a section by these maps on affine opens contained in $W$ and glue: on overlaps refine by affine opens, where compatibility was just checked. Uniqueness of sheaf gluing proves independence, compatibility with restriction, and the inverse identity. Thus these maps give an isomorphism of algebra sheaves $\mathcal O_S[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\cong B$.

proof.text: The finite-rank polynomial relative spectrum is the fibre-product affine space by [def-sbc-affine-space]. Apply the anti-equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] to the algebra-sheaf isomorphism of step 2. An equivalence and its inverse send mutually inverse maps to mutually inverse maps, so this gives the displayed isomorphism of schemes over $S$. Parts (2)--(4) of that node identify its affine restrictions with the spectra of the coefficient-preserving polynomial isomorphisms of step 2. Hence it is the canonical isomorphism specified by the standard generators. This establishes the symmetric-algebra description without identifying it by definition with the fibre-product construction.

proof.text: For the chart clauses, with $I$ arbitrary, let $\pi:\mathbb A^I_S\to S$ and $q:\mathbb A^I_S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[T_i:i\in I]$ be the two projections. For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with $U=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ and $W$ the whole second factor) identifies the open subscheme $\pi^{-1}(V)$ with $V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[T_i:i\in I]$, compatibly with the projections, and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies this with $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z[T_i:i\in I])$, the projections becoming $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $r\mapsto r\otimes1$ and $p\mapsto1\otimes p$. The ring map $R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z[T_i:i\in I]\to R[T_i:i\in I]$, $r\otimes p\mapsto rp$, is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras: its inverse is the $R$-algebra map sending $T_i\mapsto1\otimes T_i$ (universal property of the polynomial ring), and both composites fix the generators $r\otimes1$, $1\otimes T_i$, resp. $r$, $T_i$. This gives $\pi^{-1}(V)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_i:i\in I])$ over $V$, with $\pi$ induced by the inclusion of constants. For $a\in R$, $D(a)\subseteq V$ is the open subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}R_a$, embedded by $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to R_a)$ [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]. The inclusion $\pi^{-1}(D(a))\subseteq\pi^{-1}(V)$ is a morphism of affine schemes, hence $\operatorname{Spec}$ of exactly one ring map $\psi:R[T_i]\to R_a[T_i]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. It commutes with $\pi$ and with $q$, so $\psi$ restricted to $R$ is $R\to R_a$ and $\psi(T_i)=T_i$; these generate, so $\psi$ is the coefficient map fixing every $T_i$.
